title.narrative: Resilient and Strategic Transport Operational Enhancement Project in Malawi

description.narrative: The Resilient and Strategic Transport Operational Enhancement Project for Malawi has the development objective to provide safe and climate-resilient transport connectivity in the Lower Shire. Component 1: Resilient and Safe Transport Infrastructure Improvement will rehabilitate the Thabwa–Chikwawa–Bangula stretch of M1 and implement a phased upgrade of the Thabwa–Chitseko–Seven stretch of S152, improve selected markets along M1, implement systematic road safety interventions, and prepare feasibility studies for two strategic feeder roads. Sub-component 1.1 will rehabilitate approximately 90 kilometers of M1, including pavement strengthening for a 20-year design life, elevation of low sections, reconstruction of four bridges to withstand a 100-year flood return period with appropriate catchment debris management, replacement and reinforcement of undersized culverts to a 50-year return period, and stabilization of riverbanks, supported by climate-resilient design and supervision services and resettlement actions. Sub-component 1.2 will phase the upgrade of roughly 60 kilometers of S152 by reconstructing one main bridge to a 100-year flood return period, replacing and reinforcing culverts to a 50-year return period, stabilizing riverbanks, and financing climate-resilient design and supervision services and resettlement actions. Sub-component 1.3 will develop safer, climate-resilient and gender-sensitive market facilities along M1, including energy-efficient lighting, climate-reflective roofing, flood mitigation, storage, and restrooms maintained by district councils. Sub-component 1.4 will deliver road safety interventions such as pedestrian and animal crossings with speed calming, footpaths, guardrails, markings and signage, service lanes separated from traffic at markets, school-zone treatments, and community road safety education. Sub-component 1.5 will finance feasibility studies for S136 (Dyeratu–Chapananga–Mwanza) and S151 (Bangula–Ntayamoyo–Seven). Component 2: Climate-resilient Transport Asset Management will strengthen the Transport Asset Management System (AMS) by mainstreaming climate resilience across the asset lifecycle through policy and strategy improvements, updating road and bridge design standards and guidelines to reflect Malawi's climate context, and upgrading the Central Material Laboratory with equipment and training; it will also deliver a systematic capacity building program for practitioners in the Roads Authority (RA), Ministry of Transport and Public Works (MoTPW) and Road Fund Administration (RFA), and apprenticeship programs for young professionals and technicians, with measures to increase female participation and support professional registration with the Malawi Engineering Institution (MEI) in partnership with the Construction Industry Regulatory Authority of Malawi (CIRAM). Component 3: Project Management will establish and operate a Project Implementation Unit within RA, provide specialist staffing, office resources, day-to-day implementation support, and project monitoring and evaluation. Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response will enable rapid reallocation of funds to eligible emergency recovery activities upon a government declaration of emergency, submission of an Emergency Action Plan, and compliance with environmental and social requirements.
